goldens.comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.

The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.

The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.

uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:92 — A failed calendar update after guest insertion makes a retry reject every newly persisted guest, stranding the booking with unsynchronized attendees and no invitations.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real issue in the addGuests.handler.ts code. Looking at lines 85-99, the handler first persists new guests to the database (prisma.booking.update with createMany), then calls eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking). If the calendar update fails, the guests are already persisted in the database but the calendar is not synchronized. Additionally, the sendAddGuestsEmails is wrapped in try-catch that only logs errors, so emails might not be sent. On retry, the uniqueGuests filter (lines 68-72) would filter out the already-persisted guests, causing the retry to fail with 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' error. This leaves the booking in an inconsistent state with attendees in the database but not in the calendar.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:167 — Adding guests to a pending booking sends existing attendees CONFIRMED calendar requests without approval because the handler never checks booking status.

adjudication.rationale: The addGuests.handler.ts code at line 167 calls sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests) which sends calendar invites with status 'CONFIRMED' (as seen in attendee-add-guests-email.ts line 15). The handler never checks booking.status before proceeding - it only verifies the booking exists and user has permission. If a booking is in PENDING status (awaiting payment or confirmation), adding guests would send them CONFIRMED calendar invites, which is incorrect behavior. This is a real bug where the booking status should be validated before sending confirmed calendar events.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:165 — If calendar synchronization rejects after attendee creation, retrying the same guests fails uniqueness checks before synchronization or invitations can recover.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real issue in the addGuests.handler.ts code. Looking at lines 85-103, the handler first creates attendees in the database via prisma.booking.update with createMany, then later at line 165 calls eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking). If the calendar update fails, the attendees are already persisted in the database. On retry, the uniqueGuests filter at lines 71-75 will exclude these guests since they now exist in booking.attendees, causing the operation to fail with 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' error at line 78. This is a legitimate transactional consistency bug where partial failure leaves the system in an inconsistent state that cannot be recovered by retry.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:26 — Duplicated client and server guest schemas already disagree on uniqueness, so share the validation schema to prevent API callers from bypassing the dialog's duplicate-email rule.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that there are two separate validation schemas: one in AddGuestsDialog.tsx (client-side, lines 25-28) that checks for uniqueness with a refine() call, and one in addGuests.schema.ts (server-side, lines 3-6) that only validates email format without uniqueness check. This is a real architectural concern - the schemas do differ in their validation rules. However, this is not a bug because the server handler in addGuests.handler.ts (lines 68-73) does filter for unique guests against existing attendees. The finding's suggestion to share the schema is a valid code quality/maintainability concern but the current implementation doesn't have a correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5 — The unbounded guest array is materialized as bulk inserts, a full attendee reload, calendar update, and concurrent email fanout in one request, allowing a large request to exhaust database and mail capacity.

adjudication.rationale: The finding is accurate. Looking at the diff: 1) addGuests.schema.ts defines `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no size limit. 2) addGuests.handler.ts processes this unbounded array by: creating bulk inserts via `createMany`, reloading all attendees, calling `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees`, and calling `sendAddGuestsEmails` which fans out emails to all attendees. A malicious user could send thousands of guest emails in a single request, causing database strain, calendar API rate limiting, and email service exhaustion. This is a real resource exhaustion vulnerability introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/emails/email-manager.ts:541 — Each attendee checks the entire unbounded newGuests array, making guest additions quadratic and delaying mail dispatch for large events.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims there's a quadratic complexity issue at line 541 where each attendee checks the entire newGuests array. Looking at the actual code in the diff (lines 522-545), the implementation iterates through calendarEvent.attendees once and for each attendee calls newGuests.includes(attendee.email). While includes() is O(n), this results in O(attendees * newGuests) complexity, not truly quadratic in a single variable. More importantly, for typical calendar events with a handful of attendees and guests, this is completely negligible and would not 'delay mail dispatch for large events' in any meaningful way. The finding exaggerates a micro-optimization concern into a performance bug, which is not a real defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:92 — Guests are committed before calendar updates and notification delivery, so a subsequent failure leaves partial state while the existing-attendee filter prevents retrying the same guests.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a real issue in addGuests.handler.ts. Looking at lines 85-100, the code first commits guests to the database via prisma.booking.update (line 85-100), then later calls eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees (line 155) and sendAddGuestsEmails (line 160). If either of these subsequent operations fails, the guests are already persisted in the database. The uniqueGuests filter at lines 68-72 checks against existing booking.attendees, so if a retry is attempted with the same guests, they would be filtered out as duplicates since they're already in the database. This creates a partial state where guests exist in the booking but calendar/emails weren't sent, and retrying won't work.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:169 — Email failures are swallowed and reported as success without retrying, leaving newly added guests unaware of their booking invitation.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows at lines 167-171 in addGuests.handler.ts that email failures are caught and only logged ('console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")'), then the function returns success ('{ message: "Guests added" }'). This is a real concern - guests are added to the database but may never receive notification emails, and the caller has no indication of the failure. However, this is not strictly a 'bug' since the guests ARE successfully added to the booking; it's a design decision about error handling that could leave users unaware. It's an important architectural concern about silent failure handling in the new code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:54 — No test exercises the organizer, attendee, team-role, and outsider authorization branches, so a permission regression could let unauthorized users modify bookings.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces new authorization logic in addGuests.handler.ts at lines 46-54 that checks isTeamAdminOrOwner, isOrganizer, and isAttendee before allowing guest additions. This is non-trivial security-critical code. The finding correctly identifies that no tests are visible in the diff for these authorization branches. While the code itself appears to be implemented, the lack of test coverage for permission checks on a new feature that modifies bookings is a legitimate concern - a regression in this logic could allow unauthorized users to add guests to bookings they shouldn't have access to. This is a specific, actionable concern about missing test coverage for newly added security-critical logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:74 — No test covers case-insensitive existing or blacklisted addresses, so mixed-case input can bypass filtering and add duplicate or forbidden guests.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that in addGuests.handler.ts lines 68-74, the filtering logic uses direct string comparison (`guest === attendee.email` and `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`) without case normalization. While blacklistedGuestEmails are lowercased during parsing, the incoming `guest` emails are not lowercased before comparison. This means 'USER@example.com' would bypass a blacklist entry 'user@example.com', and similarly could add duplicates if existing attendees have different casing. This is a real correctness bug in the filtering logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:168 — No recipient-matrix test covers partially filtered input, so forwarding the original guest list can send existing or blacklisted attendees the wrong email template.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at line 168 in addGuests.handler.ts: `await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests);` - the code passes the original `guests` array from input, not `uniqueGuests` which was filtered to remove existing attendees and blacklisted emails. In sendAddGuestsEmails (email-manager.ts lines 522-550), this `newGuests` parameter is used to determine which email template to send: new guests get AttendeeScheduledEmail while existing attendees get AttendeeAddGuestsEmail. By passing the unfiltered `guests` instead of `uniqueGuests`, the logic `if (newGuests.includes(attendee.email))` could incorrectly match emails that were actually filtered out (existing attendees or blacklisted), potentially sending them the wrong email template.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:42 — No dialog test covers mutation errors, so the always-truthy interpolated message can expose an undefined code instead of the intended fallback error.

adjudication.rationale: The finding points to line 42 in AddGuestsDialog.tsx where the error message is constructed as `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`. If err.data is undefined or err.data.code is undefined, the string interpolation will produce 'undefined: ...' which is a poor user experience. The code uses optional chaining (err.data?.code) but still interpolates it directly into the string without a fallback, so when code is undefined, users see 'undefined' in the error message. This is a real bug in error handling logic.
